successCriteria.description: File src/shared/types/leave.types.ts exists and exports three TypeScript enums: LeaveType, LeaveRequestStatus, BalanceStatus
LeaveType enum contains exactly three members: ANNUAL, SICK, EMERGENCY
LeaveRequestStatus enum contains exactly five members: DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED
BalanceStatus enum contains exactly three members: ACTIVE, EXHAUSTED, FROZEN
The enums have zero external dependencies — no imports from other project modules or third-party libraries
Jest unit tests in tests/unit/shared/types/leave.types.test.ts verify all enum member values for LeaveType, LeaveRequestStatus, and BalanceStatus

constraints: Enums must be plain TypeScript enums (not const enums, not string literal unions) — the intent explicitly says "plain TypeScript enums"
No external dependencies — the file must not import anything from other project modules or third-party packages
Test file must be at tests/unit/shared/types/leave.types.test.ts (Jest), matching the project test framework declared in HARNESS.json
Enum member sets are scoped to this phase only: LeaveType has 3 members (not the full 6 from the reconciled architecture), BalanceStatus has 3 members (not 4)
outOfScope: Additional LeaveType members (UNPAID, MATERNITY, PATERNITY) — deferred to later phases when full policy configuration is needed
Any model, repository, service, controller, or route files — this phase is types-only
Database migrations, schema definitions, or any persistence concerns
Integration tests — only unit tests for enum value verification are in scope
Consumption of these enums by other modules (policy, balance, leave) — that begins in Phase 2

ambiguities.description: The intent says "plain TypeScript enums" but does not specify whether they should be numeric enums (default: ANNUAL=0, SICK=1, EMERGENCY=2) or string enums (ANNUAL='ANNUAL', SICK='SICK', EMERGENCY='EMERGENCY'). Both are valid "plain TypeScript enums."
